title: Atlas ownership identity, input observation, and publication boundaries
body:
## What each identity means

| Object | Observed contract and practical meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `OwnershipBody` | `kind: ownership-body`, version 1, numeric bytes. The comment explicitly preserves byte distinctions that NFC canonicalization could collapse. Preserve the reviewed UTF-8 bytes, including newlines. [T:11-16] |
| `OwnershipResult` | Body CAS hash plus `authority {scope,basis}`, `validity: supported|blocked`, `gaps`, and `evidence`. The code warns against naming validity `status` or `freshness`, since those side-index keys are excluded by existing CAS identity. Authority/validity changes matter even if prose stays equal. [T:18-30] |
| `OwnershipContract` / `OwnershipReview` | The contract contains criteria. A review names reviewer, contract hash, input hash, result hash, criteria, `pass|hold`, and provenance. A free-standing PASS cannot fill in these bindings. [T:32-48] |
| `OwnershipReceipt` | Contract hash, named `{key,version}` inputs, exact predecessor `{key,result}` pairs, and review hashes. Predecessor result identity and external input version are different relationships. [T:5-9,50-57] |
| `OwnershipArtifact` | Stable key and scope, title, layer 1-4, one of seven needs, result/receipt hashes, and navigation strings. Navigation is separately represented from receipt dependencies. [T:3,59-70] |
| `OwnershipManifest` | Scope, entries mapping keys to artifact hashes, and partial roots mapping needs to entry keys. The type permits partial roots; the protocol separately requires completeness for a claimed selection. [T:72-78; P:29-34] |

**Observed distinction:** Git blob identity and captured SHA-256 identify source or transported bytes. `observeOwnershipInput` instead returns kernel `id(...)` values for typed source/membership objects. The pilot uses `store.put(...)` to derive CAS object hashes and `id({inputs,dependencies})` to bind reviews. Those values are not interchangeable with a transport SHA-256 or a Git commit. [I:141,182; H:61,69-79,129-140; P:128-138]

**Inferred maintenance consequence:** body equality does not prove equal authority, validity, dependencies, or review. A current input hash establishes byte correspondence only; it cannot resolve a disagreement between documented intention and implemented behavior. Conversely, semantic acceptance does not establish that the live reader serves those exact accepted bytes. Keep source revision, protocol revision, runtime candidate revision, and transport commit distinct. [T:18-69; C:18,52-58; R:30-39]

authority.basis: WP-L1A source-derived evidence authored by /root/producer_l1a for execution a2095d5a-1464-4c38-a222-6376974fc9c9; code pin 1cde2ff7a71bcf7aecb5d030917b577165135d38; protocol pin ee2521a5b966bd505cc95bd1c733e09e12f33531. Observed means static source inspection; intended, inferred, and unknown are explicit. No semantic approval, runtime binding, publication, or operational authority is asserted.

gaps: Evidence scope is the five inspected code/instruction files and the pinned protocol; this is not whole-Atlas, continuity, RAG, or whole-slice coverage.

Downstream validator, trust/policy, CAS canonicalizer, persistence, coherent-read, rebuild, rollback, and recovery implementations were not inspected in this unit; only referenced contracts and call sites are described.
No live runtime input versions, generic importer execution, publication/index/read receipt, product test, CI gate, or independent consumer evidence was produced here.
Independent semantic judgments and any later runtime transformation/binding judgments are pending; absence of those judgments does not turn source-backed claims into claims of acceptance.
evidence: body.md Exact source register: source paths, line citations, Git blobs, and SHA-256 values at fixed pins.
Source evidence: ownership types T:3-152; host observer I:21-190; historical pilot H:1-158; package K:2-33; repository instructions A:156-205.
Protocol evidence: transport P:16-39,105-149; runtime R:30-65,74-127; principles C:18,24-35,52-68.
